Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a customer testimonial section for the website of a log aggregation service. Around 200 words.

## What customers say

"We were paying for three tools and still grepping through raw files when something broke. Now one query covers everything. Our median time to find the failing service went from 40 minutes to under four."
— Priya Raghunathan, SRE lead, Kettle Logistics

"The part I did not expect was the cost. We ingest about 2 TB a day, and the retention tiers let us keep 30 days hot and a year cold without a budget conversation every quarter."
— Marcus Oyelaran, platform engineering, Northwind Health

"Onboarding took an afternoon. We pointed our existing Fluent Bit agents at the new endpoint, kept our parsers, and were querying by 4 p.m. No rewrite, no migration project, no consultants."
— Dana Whitfield, director of infrastructure, Cortado Payments

"Honestly, the search syntax took our team a week to get comfortable with. It is closer to SQL than to what we had before. Once it clicked, the saved queries our on-call rotation shares now do most of the first-pass triage."
— Tobias Lind, staff engineer, Halyard Systems

"We had an outage in March that touched four regions. The correlation view put the bad config push and the error spike on the same timeline in about a minute. That is the whole reason we bought it."
— Renée Castellanos, VP engineering, Bellweather Retail

The text above has these problems. Rewrite it so none remain.
Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.

- paragraph_uniformity (5 paragraphs, spread 0.08):
